issue: #596 — the §12.7 canonical-decodability fault family (#593 owner Ruling 2). Rows first pinned here, because the family's step 01 is the only adjudication of a committed non-§5.1 preimage and a step that does not fit an L1 transaction leaves the operator escape hatch open with nothing else to notice.
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §12.7 (the fault kind, its adjudication and its boundary against §12.3's fault_item_predicate), with §5.1 for the envelope grammar, §5.4 for the per-field byte bound, §4/§7.1 for the authenticate-once hash check, §8.3/§8.4 for `K` and the tier-3 partition, and §8.8 for the carriage wire types
note:
§12.7 publishes a cost for the family's step 01 and these rows are that measurement, taken through `run-focused-check.mjs` against `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/canonical-decodability/rule.test.ak`. They split the claim the way the work splits, into a byte term and an item term, and each has a fixture-only control beside it.

**What the claim says.** Authenticate then decide: `authenticated_committed_preimage` materialises whichever §8 tier the prover named and hashes it once against §4's positionally-extracted commitment, and `envelope_verdict_v1` then walks §5.1 to a verdict, one item head per declared item. Nothing else runs — no item content is read, no §5.3/§5.5/§5.6 encoder rule is applied, no declared §2.4 length is consulted.

**The byte term.** `canonical_decodability_verdict_at_the_field_byte_bound` carries 32,768 bytes — §5.4's per-field bound, which is also `certified_chunks`' cap on a tier-3 `total_length`, so it is the largest committed preimage any carriage this family accepts can reach — as a single item on §8.4's chunked route at §8.3's `max_tier3_chunk_count` of three. It measures 1,731,640 mem / 836,726,011 cpu against a fixture-only control of 1,033,897 / 524,558,029, so the rule's own share at the byte bound is about **697,743 memory units, 5.3% of the §3.3 memory basis**, and that figure already contains the three-chunk materialisation and the one `blake2b_256` over the whole preimage. The byte axis is not where this family runs out of budget.

**The item term, and why it has controls.** `canonical_decodability_verdict_at_{two_hundred_fifty,five_hundred}_items` read the same shape at 250 and 500 minimum-width items, ungrammatical by one trailing byte — the only §5.1 refusal that costs the **whole** walk before it fires, since every other one stops at the byte that causes it. Their nets against the matching controls are 3,259,395 and 6,267,505 mem (833,809,438 and 1,595,027,125 cpu), which prices the walk at **12,032.44 mem and 3,044,870.75 cpu per item** with an intercept of 251,285 mem / 72,591,751 cpu. The §3.3 memory basis is therefore reached at about **1,076 items**; the memory axis binds, cpu at that cardinality being around 3.35G against the 8G basis. **The fit is a reading (#580, 2026-08-15; re-read under #606, 2026-08-16), and it lands on the same integer.** The crossing is bisected on the net memory axis with the pinned fork and is pinned by four selectors in the measured module (`canonical_decodability_verdict_at_the_measured_item_ceiling` and `..._at_the_first_item_over_the_basis`, each with its fixture-only control). They are deliberately **not rows here**: their raw readings are about 24.2M mem and a within-basis ledger admits only rows whose *raw* reading fits the basis. At **1,076 items** the net is **13,193,329 mem / 3,347,323,381 cpu** (row 24,201,579 / 6,722,936,444 against control 11,008,250 / 3,375,613,063); at **1,077** it is **13,205,353 mem / 3,350,363,473 cpu** (row 24,223,120 / 6,728,707,071 against control 11,017,767 / 3,378,343,598). Memory binds at the crossing exactly as published — cpu is 3.35G against the 8G basis — and the marginal cost measured across the boundary pair is 12,024 mem / 3,040,092 cpu per item, within 0.07% of the 12,032.44 the 250/500 fit gives. #580 read this crossing one item higher, at 1,077/1,078, against the pre-#606 tree; the dated paragraph at the end of this note records the move and its cause.

The controls are this ledger's one addition to §8.11's precedent, and they are not decoration. A row is a whole-test reading, and this lane's fixture is `encode_field_preimage` over a list whose length is the quantity being priced — a fold of `concat` whose own cost grows with it. Differencing the two rows alone gives 21,378 mem per item, which is within 2% of the figure §8.11's ledger publishes for the door's `walk_to_end` and would read as a coincidence rather than a measurement; nearly half of it is the producer. The controls remove it.

**The over-basis reading, and why it is not a row here.** The worst shape this family admits is §5.4's byte bound spent on minimum-width items, and §5.1's narrowest item is the *empty* one, `40`: `3 + 32,764 + 1 = 32,768` bytes carrying 32,764 items with a trailing byte, which the fit above puts at roughly **394,430,000 mem / 99,833,000,000 cpu** — 29.9x the §3.3 memory basis and 12.5x its cpu basis. It is not a row because a within-basis ledger records only `within` rows (see `exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs`), and the q1x-style `basisFit:"exceeds"` vocabulary requires an `errata` cross-reference into a normative erratum §12.7 does not yet carry. It is an **extrapolation, not a reading** — that is stated rather than glossed, and it remains the one number in this ledger that is not measured. #580 re-took it over the *measured* boundary pair rather than the 250/500 pair, which puts it at about **394,200,000 mem**, 29.9x the basis unchanged; re-derived over the #606 boundary pair it is 394,209,841 mem, the same figure at that precision. What #580 measured is the **ceiling** this figure extrapolates past (see the item term above), not the 32,764-item shape itself; closing that gap is §10's resumable walk rather than another row.

**What the residual means for the fault kind.** A committed field with more than **1,076** items cannot be adjudicated by this family in one transaction today — measured (#580, re-measured one item lower under #606), where this sentence read "roughly a thousand" before. That is a narrower hatch than the one §12.7 closes — an operator would have to commit garbage that is *also* a many-item envelope prefix — but it is a hatch, and the repair is §10's resumable walk applied to the verdict, which is #565/#579 work rather than this lane's.

**What these rows do NOT claim.** (1) That the shapes measured are valid L2 transactions. They are the worst shapes *this family* admits, which is what bounds its cost: the step authenticates bytes against the operator's own committed hash and reads no item's content. (2) A machine-checked decomposition. The within-basis shape judges absolute rows and publishes no `derived` subtraction, so every net above is arithmetic a reader does over rows this file pins, not a number the gate checks. (3) That the step-01 *validator's* thread and inclusion machinery is priced. The rows measure `committed_field_verdict_v1`, which is the family's own claim; the computation-thread and MPF membership costs it shares with every other native family are measured with those families.

Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-canonical-decodability-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement, fails in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten. Provisional on the same footing as every other ledger in this directory: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair, and the ceiling falls to 1,076.** Every row above was re-measured under the #606 batch, and the movement splits in two. Both halves are **bisected** against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits rather than assumed, and the batch's blueprint identity is unmoved throughout (md5 `5e38d7c6ccb7987d0aca710307dcaea7`, 398 validators).

(1) **A constant +9,200 mem / +1,472,000 cpu on the rule's own share, at every cardinality**, charged by the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — the constant certificate asset name, the mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality of that `field_hash` against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`. It is measured to be constant rather than fitted to be: both cardinality rows moved by exactly that amount while their fixture-only controls did not move by a unit; the marginal across the boundary pair is the same 12,024 mem / 3,040,092 cpu per item #580 measured; and only the intercept rose (242,085 → 251,285 mem, 71,119,751 → 72,591,751 cpu). The pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` costs this family nothing — its readings are identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit — and nothing after `d528e00b` moves these rows. What is **not** published here is a decomposition: these rows carry `Inline` tier-1 carriage at a body field, so the certificate branch is not what they execute, and which of the repair's changes to the compiled door carries how much of the constant is not settled by these readings.

**The consequence is the point, and it is a downward correction.** #580's margin at 1,077 items was 3,847 memory units, and a constant +9,200 consumes it: 1,077 now nets 13,205,353 mem and is **over** the §3.3 basis. The crossing was re-bisected on the net memory axis with the pinned fork, the four boundary selectors were re-pinned at 1,076 / 1,077 in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/canonical-decodability/rule.test.ak`, and the published single-transaction ceiling moves **down one item, 1,077 → 1,076**. §12.7's operator escape hatch is one item wider than the spec currently says until the docs half of this batch moves with it. The 250/500 fit re-derived at the new intercept lands on 1,076 as well, so fit and reading still agree.

(2) **+200 mem / +32,000 cpu on the byte-bound row alone**, charged by `3eb41df7` (the §8.6 certificate field-index bound routed through `field_count`) and measured at `2a64d6f9` → `3eb41df7` with the fixture-only control unmoved. It is paid once per door opening that decodes a certificate datum, which is why only the tier-3 row here sees it and why the same +200 / +32,000 appears on all six tier-3 door rows of `native-tx-carriage-exec-ledger-v1.json`. This half arrived **after** the batch's first ledger re-take (`7158377e`) and left three ledgers red until this re-take; that is recorded rather than quietly absorbed. The byte-bound row's whole movement from the pre-batch 1,737,095 / 803,933,814 is therefore **−5,455 mem / +32,792,197 cpu**, and its net share is now about 697,743 memory units — 5.3% of the basis, the same figure this note published before.

No `basisFit` moved: every row here was and remains `within`. The neutralisation selectors were re-run green with the rows, and the ceiling shape guard `canonical_decodability_measured_ceiling_shape_is_the_cardinality_rows_shape` held across the move, which is what makes this a re-reading of the same shape rather than a re-pinning of a cheaper one.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24.

modules.neutralisationNote: Both selectors are mutation-verified rather than assumed. (1) `canonical_decodability_ledger_fixture_sits_at_the_field_byte_bound` is the shape guard, and it is why a re-take cannot quietly re-pin a cheaper row: it asserts the bound fixture is exactly `max_transaction_aggregate_field_bytes` bytes, above §8.3's `K`, at `expected_chunk_count == max_tier3_chunk_count`, ungrammatical for the trailing-byte reason the whole-walk claim depends on, and a single item; and that both cardinality fixtures fit tier 1 and differ in item count alone. Shrink any of them and this selector goes red before the row is re-pinned. (2) `canonical_decodability_verdict_refuses_substituted_certified_chunks` is the discrimination guard: neutralising `expect field_commitment(preimage) == expected_hash` in `authenticated_committed_preimage` (`lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak`) turns it red, and the check report names that exact line as the failure it traps. The vector is honest about isolating that one guard — the certificate is one a real certification produced, its digest vector is over the real chunks, every named chunk is the right length and the count is the derived one — so every §8.4/§8.6 check `certified_chunks` runs still passes and only §4's hash separates the substituted bytes from the committed ones. It is also what makes the bound row's tier-3 carriage falsifiable: without that check the manifest would be authenticating the preimage, and a manifest is minted against a `witness_set_hash` its own redeemer supplied. The family's other guards — the §2.5 body/witness pairing, the fabricated verdict and field index, the forged transactions root, the honest-block negative — are covered by the small-shape selectors in the two validator modules, because a 32,768-byte fixture isolates none of them better than a six-byte one does.
